    StartersGalley bread rollsSoft milk rolls brushed with butter and flaky saltHow to make it500g bread flour7g dried yeast300ml warm milk50g butter, softened, for the dough2 tbsp caster sugar1 egg20g butter, melted, for brushing1 tsp flaky saltMix the flour, yeast, milk, butter, sugar and egg into a soft dough and knead.Prove until doubled.Shape into rolls.Prove again.Bake at 190°C.Brush with the melted butter and flaky salt.Saffron rouille and prawn crostiniToasted baguette with garlic, saffron rouille and a poached prawn, from the captain's birthday dinnerHow to make it1 pinch saffron threads1 egg yolk2 garlic cloves, 1 crushed and 1 halved1 chilli flakes1 lemon, zested and juiced150ml olive oil16 green prawns, peeled with tails on1 baguette1 fennel bulb with frondSoak the saffron in 1 tbsp hot water for 5 minutes.Whisk the egg yolk with the crushed garlic, saffron water, chilli and 1 tsp lemon juice, then whisk in the olive oil a few drops at a time until thick. Season with salt.Poach the prawns in simmering salted water for 2 minutes until just pink, then cool.Slice the baguette into 16 rounds and toast at 200°C for 6 minutes, then rub each with the cut garlic.Spread with rouille, top with a prawn, a few fennel fronds and lemon zest.MainsRyback's spit-free bouillabaisseSaffron fish stew with rouille and toasted baguetteHow to make it1 fennel bulb1 leek1 onion3 garlic cloves2 tbsp olive oil1 pinch saffron2 strips of orange peel1 tin chopped tomatoes (400g)1 L fish stock500g firm white fish fillets500g mussels300g prawns2 garlic cloves, for the rouille1 egg yolk125ml olive oil, for the rouille1 lemon1 baguetteChop the fennel, leek, onion and garlic.Soften in oil with the saffron, orange peel and tomatoes.Add the fish stock and simmer.Add the fish, then the mussels and prawns, and cook until the shells open.For the rouille, crush the garlic with a pinch of salt, whisk in the egg yolk and a few saffron threads soaked in a spoon of the hot broth, then whisk in the olive oil drop by drop until thick. Finish with a squeeze of lemon.Toast sliced baguette and serve with the rouille.Navy galley glazed meatloaf and mashGet my pies out of the oven!How to make itAs written, serves 4Beef and pork meatloaf with a sticky tomato and brown sugar glaze, sliced thick over buttery mash with peas and onion gravy.Soak 60g breadcrumbs in 80ml milk.Mix with 500g beef mince, 300g pork mince, 1 grated onion, 1 egg, 2 tbsp Worcestershire and salt.Shape in a lined loaf tin.Mix 80ml tomato sauce with 2 tbsp brown sugar, spread on top and bake at 180°C for 1 hour.Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml hot milk.Fry 1 sliced onion, stir in 1 tbsp flour and 300ml beef stock for gravy.Cook 300g frozen peas.SweetsCaptain's birthday cakeVanilla layer cake piped Happy Birthday Captain in blueHow to make it200g butter, softened, for the cake200g caster sugar4 eggs200g self-raising flour250g butter, softened, for icing400g icing sugar1/4 tsp blue food colouringHeat the oven to 175°C and line two tins. Beat the butter and sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour.Bake.Cool completely.Beat the butter and icing sugar for the buttercream.Fill and cover the cake.Tint a little buttercream blue with the food colouring and pipe the message.DrinksUSS Missouri navy grogDark rum and white rum shaken with lime, grapefruit and honey syrup, poured over crushed ice with a lime wheel and a dusting of nutmeg.How to make it2 tbsp honey2 tbsp hot water90ml dark rum90ml white rum3 limes60ml grapefruit juice1 tray ice1 tray crushed ice1 whole nutmeg, to grateDissolve the honey in the hot water.Shake both rums, lime juice, grapefruit juice and the honey syrup with ice.Strain into tumblers packed with crushed ice.Add a lime wheel to each and grate a little nutmeg on top.
